Authentication

1. Authentication in Ignite
  • By default, Ignite has no authentication — any client or node can connect to the cluster;
  • For production, you should enable authentication to restrict who can join the cluster and access data;
  • Ignite supports thin client authentication and node authentication;
2. Enabling Thin Client Authentication
  • Requires persistence to be enabled (credentials are stored persistently): 
    DataStorageConfiguration storageCfg = new DataStorageConfiguration();
storageCfg.getDefaultDataRegionConfiguration().setPersistenceEnabled(true);

IgniteConfiguration cfg = new IgniteConfiguration();
cfg.setDataStorageConfiguration(storageCfg);
cfg.setAuthenticationEnabled(true);
  • Default user: ignite / ignite;
  • Connecting with credentials: 
    ClientConfiguration clientCfg = new ClientConfiguration()
    .setAddresses("host:10800")
    .setUserName("myuser")
    .setUserPassword("mypassword");
3. Managing Users
  • Use SQL to manage users once connected as an admin: 
    -- Create a new user
ALTER USER "newuser" WITH PASSWORD 'securePassword123';

-- Change password
ALTER USER "newuser" WITH PASSWORD 'newSecurePassword456';

-- Drop a user
DROP USER "newuser";
4. Custom Authentication SPI
  • For integration with external identity providers (LDAP, OAuth, etc.), implement a custom security plugin;
  • GridGain (commercial distribution) provides built-in LDAP integration;
  • The open-source version supports custom authentication via plugin SPI;
5. JDBC Authentication
  • Pass credentials via the JDBC connection string: 
    String url = "jdbc:ignite:thin://host:10800?user=myuser&password=mypassword";
Connection conn = DriverManager.getConnection(url);
